events.title: Patrick Henry's "Give Me Liberty" Speech
events.description: Addressing the Virginia convention, Patrick Henry urged the colony to arm its militia against Britain. His speech is traditionally remembered for the line "give me liberty, or give me death!"
events.significance: The speech became one of the best-known rallying cries of the American Revolution. It still stands as a symbol of the fight for freedom.

events.title: Great Earthquake Destroys Inwa
events.description: A massive earthquake struck central Burma and devastated Inwa (Ava), the former capital of the Konbaung dynasty.
events.significance: The quake left the old royal city in ruins. Inwa never recovered its former status, which changed the political and cultural geography of Myanmar.

events.title: The First Passenger Elevator Is Installed
events.description: Elisha Otis's safety elevator was installed at a department store at 488 Broadway in New York City.
events.significance: Otis's safety design made tall buildings practical. It paved the way for modern skyscrapers and the cities we know today.

events.title: Mussolini Founds the Fascist Movement
events.description: In Milan, Benito Mussolini launched his Fascist political movement, bringing together a small group of followers.
events.significance: The movement grew into the Fascist regime that ruled Italy from 1922. It became a model for authoritarian movements elsewhere in Europe.

events.title: The Reichstag Passes the Enabling Act
events.description: Germany's Reichstag passed the Enabling Act, which let Adolf Hitler's government make laws without parliamentary approval. It was published the next day.
events.significance: The act removed the Weimar Republic's constitutional checks and legally underpinned the Nazi dictatorship.
